title: 9 Retail Benchmarks for Brands To Know in 2027
summary: Learn how retail benchmarks help compare your performance against industry averages, plus how to set relevant benchmarks for your brand.
body_markdown:
Retail benchmarks are standards for measuring and comparing retail business performance so retailers can identify areas for improvement. Internal benchmarks compare performance across different periods or areas of your business, while external benchmarks compare your performance against broader industry standards and competitors in your market.


Tracking your own profit over time shows whether your business is improving, but it doesn’t tell you how your performance compares with other retailers. According to 2026 data from[NYU Stern School of Business](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/margin.html) , publicly traded grocery and food retail businesses average a 1.32% net profit margin, compared with 7.84% for building supply retailers.


You might be pleased with your results based on internal metrics, but external benchmarks can reveal gaps between your business and industry peers. It can prompt you to explore potential improvements for exceeding customer expectations. Learn which key benchmarks to monitor, how top performers evaluate store performance, and how to use Shopify Analytics to fine-tune your business strategy.


## What are external retail benchmarks?


External[benchmarking](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-benchmarking) involves comparing your performance against industry averages, direct competitors, and the wider retail market. This benchmarking data can reveal strengths and weaknesses that internal metrics alone might not uncover.


Industry standards vary across retail sectors, business models, product categories, and fulfillment setups. For instance, customer acquisition cost benchmarks for an apparel brand selling[direct-to-consumer (DTC)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-direct-to-consumer) may differ from those of an[omnichannel](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/omnichannel-marketing) home goods brand. Comparing your results with relevant businesses can help you identify performance gaps worth investigating.


Alistair Marshall, head of retail and visual merchandising for the UK-based apparel group[TFG Brands](https://www.tfglondon.com/) (whose portfolio includes Hobbs, Whistles, Phase Eight, and Inside Story), says external benchmarks can help retailers identify opportunities for improvement. For example, comparing sales per square foot against other stores in the same shopping center can reveal differences in performance worth investigating.


“If people are driving higher densities off their space, what are they doing that we’re not doing?” Alistair says. “Is that because of the store layout? Is that because of the product selection? Is that because of the price point that we have?” Having comprehensive data can help brands answer these questions and make improvements.

## Common retail industry benchmarks


- Gross margin
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
- Customer lifetime value (LTV)
- Return on ad spend (ROAS)
- Average order value (AOV)
- Online and in-store conversion rate
- Returning customer rate
- Sell-through rate
- Sales per square foot


External benchmarks provide targets for evaluating company performance across ecommerce and physical retail. Before auditing your performance against industry standards, consider which[key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-kpi) are most relevant to your business. Here are nine to consider:


### Gross margin


[Gross margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/gross-margin) reflects the share of total sales revenue your business retains after deducting[cost of goods sold (COGS)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cost-of-goods-sold) . Benchmark targets vary by[product category](https://www.shopify.com/blog/product-category) . NYU Stern School of Business reports a 26.31% average gross margin for publicly traded grocery and food retailers and 56.88% for apparel companies.


Alistair says retailers should account for planned markdowns when setting margin targets. Rather than waiting until the end of a season to discount slow-selling merchandise, he favors smaller discounts earlier.


“It’s way better for me to do a 20%-off weekend to shift slow-selling lines in season than to keep leaving it on the floor at full price, it doesn’t sell, and end up discounting it 40% or 50% or 60% down the line,” he says.


### Customer acquisition cost (CAC)


[Customer acquisition cost](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-acquisition-cost) is the average sales and marketing expense required to acquire a new customer. External CAC benchmarks help you evaluate marketing effectiveness, although acquisition costs vary by channel, product category, and competition.


Rather than targeting an arbitrary dollar figure, you can evaluate CAC relative to the revenue generated by a customer’s first purchase and the total revenue they’re expected to generate over the course of their relationship with your business.


According to an analysis by[First Page Sage](https://firstpagesage.com/reports/average-cac-by-industry-b2c-edition/) , CAC costs for ecommerce businesses averaged $64 through organic channels and $68 through paid channels.


### Customer lifetime value (LTV)


[Customer lifetime value](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-lifetime-value) measures the total revenue a customer generates throughout their relationship with your store. You can compare LTV with CAC to understand how much customers spend relative to what it costs to acquire them. Because product prices and purchasing habits vary widely, useful benchmarks depend on the type of retail business.


According to 2026 research published by[Digital Applied](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/customer-lifetime-value-benchmarks-2026-industry-data) , the median LTV-to-CAC ratio was estimated at 3.6:1 for DTC apparel businesses, 3.2:1 for DTC beauty businesses, and 4.1:1 for DTC subscription consumables.


Alistair emphasizes the importance of[customer retention](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-a-good-customer-retention-rate) in increasing LTV. “How can we take a one-time customer into a two-time customer?” he says. “Because as you get her back in more frequently, you naturally increase the lifetime value of that customer, and each incremental transaction is generally bigger. Loyal customers spend more with you; it’ll be a higher average transaction.”


### Return on ad spend (ROAS)


[Return on ad spend](https://www.shopify.com/blog/roas) calculates the revenue generated for every dollar spent on paid advertising. It helps you evaluate the effectiveness of your promotional investment in paid ads. A 3:1 ROAS, for example, means a campaign generates $3 in revenue for every $1 spent on ads.


According to 2026 data from[Triple Whale](https://www.triplewhale.com/blog/whats-a-good-roas) , the median ROAS across brands using its platform was 2.22:1. Benchmarks vary by retail category and advertising channel. For example, apparel and accessories brands achieved a median ROAS of 3.88:1 on Google Ads, compared with 2.26:1 on Meta Ads.


Acceptable ROAS targets also depend heavily on margins. A brand with 80% margins before advertising costs can afford a lower ROAS than a brand with a 50% margin, assuming other costs are comparable.


### Average order value (AOV)


[Average order value](https://www.shopify.com/blog/average-order-value) (also called[average transaction value](https://www.shopify.com/blog/average-transaction-value) in physical retail) measures customer average spend per order or transaction. According to ecommerce benchmark data from[Dynamic Yield](https://marketing.dynamicyield.com/benchmarks/average-order-value/) , global average order value is $182, although figures vary considerably by product category. In September 2026, for example, AOVs were $62 for consumer goods, $124 for multibrand retail, and $390 for fashion, accessories, and apparel.


You can track AOV alongside units per transaction (UPT) to evaluate sales effectiveness and promotional pricing. In physical storefronts, product displays and staff recommendations can encourage customers to purchase additional items.


Alistair emphasizes making it easier for shoppers to purchase complementary items, such as pieces that complete an outfit. “Are you making the outfit building really easy for her? Are you making the experience really easy? What does that fitting room look like?” he says, as an example.


### Online and in-store conversion rate


[Conversion rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sales-conversion-rate) measures the percentage of visits that result in a purchase, whether online or in a physical store. According to benchmark data from[IRP Commerce](https://www.irpcommerce.com/en/gb/EcommerceMarketData.aspx) , the average ecommerce conversion rate among stores on its platform was 1.97% in September 2026.


For physical retail, benchmarks vary by store type. According to 2026 guidance from the retail analytics provider[Dor](https://www.getdor.com/blog/2026/04/28/what-is-a-retail-conversion-rate-the-complete-guide-for-store-owners/) , typical in-store conversion rates range from 15% to 25% for apparel and fashion retailers, compared with 5% to 12% for luxury retailers.


Alistair also emphasizes how conversion rates depend on a retailer’s market positioning. “A Forever 21, a Zara, is going to be very different from a Dior, a Rodeo Drive–esque store,” he says. Alistair considers a 30% in-store conversion rate impressive, but says 20% may be achievable for an appointment-driven luxury brand, while 10% to 15% is realistic for a shopping center fashion store.


The length of the buying cycle can also affect conversion. Alistair describes how a customer shopping for a special-occasion dress might visit several times before making a purchase. “She might come in on her own, see the dress she wants for her wedding, then leave,” he says. “She might come back with a girlfriend and look at it again, then leave. Then she’ll come back with family, and she might purchase.”


### Returning customer rate


The returning customer rate measures the percentage of customers who have made more than one purchase with your brand. According to[TrueProfit](https://trueprofit.io/blog/what-is-a-good-returning-customer-rate) , a healthy returning customer rate falls between 20% and 40%.


Alistair emphasizes that appropriate benchmarks depend on how frequently customers are likely to need new products. “On a 12-month rolling cycle, getting 20% of your customers to return is a pretty good statistic,” he says.


Personalized outreach can help improve customer satisfaction by making recommendations more relevant to individual shoppers, encouraging repeat purchases. “You’ve got to be really discerning, and personalized, to cut through all that noise,” Alistair says. He recalls how 20% of fashion retailer Theory’s business in the US came from sales associates contacting customers with personalized recommendations through the Tulip clienteling platform.


### Sell-through rate


[Sell-through rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sell-through-rate) is an inventory management metric that measures the amount of inventory sold within a specific reporting period compared to the inventory received from suppliers. A common sell-through benchmark for fashion retailers is 60% to 80%, according to fashion analytics firm[Heuritech](https://heuritech.com/articles/sell-through-fashion/) .


When a style lags behind its target, cutting prices shouldn’t necessarily be your first response. “There’s so much you can do before you need to start pricing it down,” says Alistair. He recommends giving slow-selling styles more prominent placement, having sales associates wear them on the shop floor, and offering staff incentives to encourage sales.


### Sales per square foot


[Sales per square foot](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/sales-per-square-foot) measures the average revenue generated per square foot of physical retail space. It’s a common measure of store performance and merchandising effectiveness, but benchmarks vary considerably by retail category. These examples illustrate differences across retail formats:


-


**Home improvement.**[Lowe’s](https://corporate.lowes.com/investors/financial-information/annual-reports-proxy-statements) generated about $440 in annual net sales per square foot in fiscal 2025.


-


**General merchandise.**[Walmart](https://stock.walmart.com/financial-information/annual-reports) US generated approximately $691 per square foot in fiscal 2026.


-


**Beauty and personal care.**[Bath & Body Works](https://investors.bbwinc.com/financial-reporting/annual-reports) reported $1,026 in sales per average selling square foot in 2025.


-


**Grocery.**[Village Super Market](https://www.annualreports.com/Company/village-super-market-inc) reported $1,562 in same-store sales per average square foot of selling space in fiscal 2026.


Retailers should also consider store size, location, and operating costs when comparing performance. “I have a store that has the highest pounds per square foot, because it’s just a small store on a really busy street,” says Alistair. “So yes, that’s incredible, but it doesn’t mean that the team’s amazing. It doesn’t mean that the product selection is amazing.”


He notes that a store with lower sales per square foot could be more profitable if it has higher conversion rates and lower rent. “No retailer should look at any KPI in isolation,” he says.


## How to use Shopify to set internal retail benchmarks


- Review behavior and conversion funnels
- Monitor inventory health and turnover
- Benchmark physical stores with Shopify POS


Establishing reliable internal benchmarks starts with reviewing historical sales data in your Shopify admin. Shopify Analytics provides reports that help you track performance, compare results across sales channels and store locations, identify areas for improvement, and measure success over time.


Here’s how you can use this information to establish baselines for the retail benchmarks discussed above and support continuous improvement:


### Review behavior and conversion funnels


To track online conversion rates, open the[conversion rate over time](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/behaviour-reports#online-store-conversion-over-time) report in[Shopify Analytics](https://www.shopify.com/analytics) . This report shows how many shopping sessions result in customers adding products to their carts, reaching checkout, and completing a purchase.


Use historical data to establish your store’s baseline conversion rate, then compare results over time to identify changes in customer behavior. Reviewing where shoppers leave the conversion funnel can help you identify performance gaps—such as drop-offs during checkout—that need further investigation.


### Monitor inventory health and turnover


[Shopify inventory reports](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/inventory-reports) help you track sell-through rates, days of inventory remaining, and product performance. Use the[products by sell-through rate](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/inventory-reports#product-sell-through-rate) report to identify how much inventory you’ve sold over a reporting period and compare results over time. You can also use[ABC analysis](https://www.shopify.com/blog/abc-analysis) , which grades products based on revenue contribution, to identify your top products and prioritize restocking decisions.


### Benchmark physical stores with Shopify POS


For physical retail locations,[Shopify POS](https://www.shopify.com/pos) integrates with Shopify Analytics to help retailers compare sales performance across stores. Use retail sales reports to track sales by location and identify changes over time. You can also combine store sales data with each location’s selling floor area to calculate sales per square foot and compare results against your internal benchmarks.


## Retail benchmarks FAQ


### What are the five KPIs in retail?


Five commonly used key performance indicators for retail are sales revenue, gross margin, average order or transaction value, customer acquisition cost, and inventory turnover.


### What are some examples of key benchmarks?


Common retail benchmarks include a 60% to 80% sell-through rate for fashion retailers and a 20% to 40% returning customer rate, although appropriate targets vary by business. Triple Whale reported a median return on ad spend of 2.22:1 among brands using its platform in 2026. Retailers can also compare sales per square foot against similar businesses.


### What are the seven types of benchmarking?


A common classification of benchmarking includes seven types: internal, competitive, strategic, performance, process, functional, and generic. These approaches allow you to compare performance within your business or against other businesses to help improve overall company results and strengthen long-term profitability.
